content:
Launch Sunday is for the people you hope will make this church their home: neighbors, coworkers, friends and the guests your team has invited. Plan the day around them.

Invite one partner representative from your sending church or network to take part in the service, for example a short greeting or a prayer. Ask 6–8 weeks ahead, and see [Partner Organization Coordination](/wiki/launch-sunday/partner-organization-coordination) for the steps.

Ask your other supporters, such as family, financial partners and friends from other churches, to pray for you that morning and to visit on the second or third Sunday. Many church plants see attendance dip in the weeks after launch, and a visit then encourages your team when it helps most. Tell them why you're asking, so no one feels turned away, and give them the dates.

If supporters come on Launch Sunday anyway, welcome them warmly. The goal is a clear invitation, not a rule.

---

## Why this invitation plan

Launch Sunday is planned around the people you hope will make this church their home. Your supporters already care about this church plant, and they can help in two ways: by praying for you on Launch Sunday and by visiting on the second or third Sunday. Asking them to come later is not a sign that they are unwelcome. It gives their visit a clear purpose.

One partner representative still has a place on Launch Sunday itself. A short greeting or a prayer from your sending church or network gives your partners a clear part in the day, while the rest of the room stays focused on your guests.

---

## What to tell supporters

Tell your supporters the plan early, in your own words, and tell them why you're asking. A clear explanation helps no one feel turned away.

When you write to them or talk with them, include:

- A request to pray for you and your team on Launch Sunday morning
- The dates of the second and third Sundays, with an invitation to visit on one of them
- Thanks for the support they have already given
- A warm word that anyone who still comes on Launch Sunday will be welcomed

<Callout type="tip">
  Give supporters the second- and third-Sunday dates in writing, so they can
  plan their visit and pray for you on Launch Sunday.
</Callout>

---

## How this works with partner churches

Partner churches follow the same plan. Invite one partner representative to take part in the Launch Sunday service, and ask 6–8 weeks ahead. [Partner Organization Coordination](/wiki/launch-sunday/partner-organization-coordination) walks through the steps, from the first request to the thank-you after launch.

When a partner church announces your launch to its congregation, ask it to pray on Launch Sunday and to invite people who want to visit to come on the second or third Sunday. Give it those dates, so the announcement and your own invitations say the same thing.

For how this plan fits the rest of the day, see [The 5 Priority Details for Launch Sunday](/wiki/launch-sunday/5-priority-details).

---

## When supporters come anyway

Some supporters will come on Launch Sunday anyway. Welcome them warmly and thank them for coming. The plan is a clear invitation, not a rule, and no one should be turned away at the door.

<Callout type="scripture">
  *"I thank my God in all my remembrance of you, always offering prayer with joy in my every prayer for you all, because of your fellowship in the gospel from the first day until now."* — Philippians 1:3-5 (LSB)
</Callout>

Ask your supporters to pray on Launch Sunday and to visit on the second or third Sunday, invite one partner representative to take part in the service, and plan the day around your guests.

It still needs a source, or Sebastian's explicit confirmation as human author that it stands as his general observation, before it can pass. Apart from that sentence and the tier C minimums, the draft holds.
